page: Microsoft Azure D96a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating up to 3.35 GHz. The instance provisions 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory totals 384.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as 2,577 GB of direct SSD space, while hardware GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark data illustrates a balance between broad multithreaded capacity and moderate single-core speeds. In compute tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks reached 68,614.68, aided by a top-tier score of 96,989.58 in encryption operations via hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. Extended instructions and ray tracing benchmarks scored within the upper quartile, and Clang software compilation reached 41,902.0. However, raw single-core throughput under stress-ng fell into the bottom tier at 782.09, reflecting clock speed limitations inherent to high-core density CPUs of this architecture generation.

Memory and caching subsystems yield strong multi-threaded compression metrics, registering 405.92 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and a small-block cached read bandwidth of 3,919.03 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read and write bandwidths measure at 156.51 GB/sec and 78.13 GB/sec respectively. In database operations, the instance handles 71.11 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by its substantial memory capacity and bundled NVMe-class SSD storage.

From an efficiency perspective, the D96a_v4 delivers massive thread density and bundled high-capacity local SSD space within a balanced general-purpose allocation. Tradeoffs center on lower per-thread serial throughput and the absence of advanced vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX. The instance profile fits large-scale parallel compilation, container hosting, multi-threaded data processing, in-memory caching platforms, and distributed database services.
